chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in sleep what a man sees. He said: If she emits, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon her; and if she does not emit, then ghusl is not obligatory upon her.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.أَنْزَلَتْ: she emitted fluid, which triggers the ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath that becomes obligatory upon emission
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep or dream-state in which the experience occurs
key_terms.تُنْزِلْ: she does not emit fluid, in which case no ghusl is required

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl after seeing a sexual dream?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory for a woman after a sexual dream only if emission occurs. If no emission occurs, then ghusl is not required. It establishes parity in the principle of ritual purity based on actual emission.
